results.quote: For triangle listing, where every triangle in the graph is output by at least one of its nodes, the worst case energy complexity is $\Omega\big(n^{1/3}/logn\big)$ rounds for algorithms that fail with some small constant probability $\epsilon>0$.

For local triangle listing, which requires every node to output all triangles that it is part of, we obtain a lower bound of $\Omega(n/logn)$ that holds even for the expected node-averaged energy complexity.

For s-clique listing, where every s-clique in the graph is output by at least one of its nodes, the worst case energy complexity is $\Omega\big(n^{1-2/s}/logn\big)$ rounds for algorithms that fail with some small constant probability $\epsilon>0$.
Computing an exact minimum vertex cover, maximum independent set, or minimum dominating set has a node-averaged energy complexity of $\Omega\big(\frac{n^2}{log^2n}\big)$ in expectation.
Computing an exact minimum vertex cover, maximum independent set, or minimum dominating set has a node-averaged energy complexity of $\Omega\big(\frac{n^2}{log^2n}\big)$ in expectation.

Computing the exact network diameter with $\epsilon$ error, for some small constant $\epsilon>0$, has a node-averaged energy complexity of $\Omega(n/logn)$ in expectation.
The same bound holds for computing exact all-pair-shortest-paths (APSP) routing tables.

In any undirected, weighted graph G, or directed, unweighted graph G, computing the exact Minimum Weight Cycle with $\epsilon$ error, for some small constant $\epsilon>0$, has a node-averaged energy complexity of $\Omega(n/logn)$ in expectation.
